title: Log determinant of a positive definite matrix: absolute error
summary: Estimate $\tau=\log\det(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\log A)$, with the matrix logarithm defined by spectral decomposition.

task.description_zh: Estimate $\tau=\log\det(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\log A)$, with the matrix logarithm defined by spectral decomposition.
description_paragraphs: Estimate $\tau=\log\det(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\log A)$, with the matrix logarithm defined by spectral decomposition.

model.instance: The unknown real matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is symmetric positive definite. The information $0<\mu\le\beta$, $\mu I\preceq A\preceq\beta I$, and $\beta/\mu\le\kappa$ is public.

assumptions.description: A is positive definite with spectrum in the public interval [mu,beta] and kappa(A)<=kappa.

model.description_zh: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0$ and $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, with $\mu I\preceq A\preceq\beta I$, $0<\mu\le\beta$, and $\beta/\mu\le\kappa$.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0$ and $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, with $\mu I\preceq A\preceq\beta I$, $0<\mu\le\beta$, and $\beta/\mu\le\kappa$.

operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.
oracle.description_zh: The information $d,\mu,\beta,\kappa,\eta,\delta$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Query $v\in\mathbb R^d$ returns exact $Av$. Neither $\log(A)v$ nor a shifted inverse action is available for free.
description_paragraphs: The information $d,\mu,\beta,\kappa,\eta,\delta$ is public and $A$ is hidden. Query $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$. Neither $\log(A)v$ nor a shifted inverse action is available for free.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Recover the $d$ columns of $A$ by standard basis queries. Its positive spectrum permits exact internal evaluation of the sum of eigenvalue logarithms. The log-determinant error is zero, regardless of whether the log determinant itself is positive, zero, or negative.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.supports: The Rademacher construction avoids the additional Gaussian sample-count restriction in Theorem 19. The sampling bound in Lemma 21 does not depend on the sign of the log determinant.

conditions: B=log A may be indefinite. A Bv call is not automatically free, and the error and target normalization must be checked again.
relations.error_map: The original trace error is $\epsilon\|\log A\|_{S_p}$. To make it at most $\eta$, use a known valid norm bound and a budget for simulation error.
relations.oracle_simulation: The action $Bv$ may be approximated by polynomials or Lanczos; it is not one exact $Av$ call. The included argument covers the SLQ quadratic-form route only.

components.cost: Each simulation costs the approximation degree for h = log. Trace upper and lower bounds do not transfer one for one.
